introHeading: A booth built for Brooklyn's loft and rooftop scene
introParas: Step inside the Vogue booth's three-dimensional, LED-lined backdrop and a finished video is ready in about ten seconds — a boomerang, a short clip or an animated GIF, guest's choice. That turnaround matters in a borough where a lot of our bookings are the kind of night where the DJ doesn't stop and nobody wants to leave the dance floor to stand still for a photo. The LED interior surrounds guests with light rather than sitting behind them, which is exactly the effect that reads best in the dim, moody rooms common at Bushwick warehouse parties and Williamsburg loft receptions.

Because the structure is larger than a mirror booth, load-in logistics matter more here than almost anywhere else we work. We've carried road cases up the narrow stairwells of Park Slope brownstones and through freight elevators in Bushwick's converted warehouses, and we plan the vogue booth's placement around whichever one your venue has before we show up. It needs a minimum of 8ft x 8ft of clear floor — 12ft x 12ft is better if the room allows it — at least 7.5ft of ceiling clearance, and a dedicated 15 or 20 amp outlet. At venues with restricted freight access, tell us early and we will confirm the fit and budget closer to two hours for load-in rather than the twenty minutes a mirror booth needs.

The vogue booth is our most-booked choice for Sweet Sixteens, brand launches and nightlife-style events, and Brooklyn supplies plenty of all three — DUMBO product launches with a skyline view, Crown Heights and Bay Ridge Sweet Sixteens with a full dance floor, Greenpoint bar takeovers running past midnight. There's no travel fee anywhere in Brooklyn, so whether your venue is a Gowanus event space or a Downtown Brooklyn hotel ballroom, the quote you get is the number you pay.

faqHeading: Vogue Video Booth in Brooklyn — FAQ

faqs.q: How much space does the vogue booth need at a Brooklyn loft or warehouse venue?
faqs.a: A minimum of 8ft x 8ft of clear floor, 12ft x 12ft if the room allows it, with at least 7.5ft of ceiling clearance and a dedicated 15 or 20 amp outlet. Bushwick warehouses and Williamsburg lofts usually have the ceiling height to spare — it's more often a Park Slope brownstone parlor floor where we need to talk through the footprint in advance.

faqs.q: How long does load-in take for the vogue booth?
faqs.a: Longer than our mirror or glam booths, which take about 20 minutes. The vogue booth's structure means budgeting closer to two hours at venues with restricted freight access — a real factor in Bushwick's converted warehouses and any Brooklyn building without a loading dock. Tell us your venue early and we'll confirm the timeline before you book.

faqs.q: Do you charge a travel fee anywhere in Brooklyn?
faqs.a: No. There's no travel fee anywhere in Brooklyn, from Bay Ridge to Greenpoint. We quote it from your venue ZIP code before you book so there's nothing to discover on the invoice afterward.

faqs.q: What kind of Brooklyn venues have you set the vogue booth up in?
faqs.a: Warehouse spaces in Bushwick, rooftop venues in Williamsburg and DUMBO with the skyline behind the booth, brownstone gardens in Park Slope, and event floors in Downtown Brooklyn. Send us your venue name on the quote form and we'll tell you exactly what fits the room.

faqs.q: Can the LED interior match our event's color scheme?
faqs.a: Yes. The lighting inside the backdrop is programmable, so we can set it to your palette or brand colors before doors open — a common request for Crown Heights and Bay Ridge Sweet Sixteens built around a specific theme color.

faqs.q: Does the vogue booth print photos, or is it video-only?
faqs.a: It's primarily a video and GIF booth, but guests can choose to print a still from their session too, so you get both a shareable clip and something physical to take home.

faqs.q: Is an attendant included with the vogue booth rental?
faqs.a: Yes. A trained attendant runs the booth for the full length of your rental — managing the queue, keeping the session moving, and packing everything down at the end of the night. You don't need to assign anyone from your own team to it.

faqs.q: Do you carry insurance and can you provide a COI for our Brooklyn venue?
faqs.a: Yes. We carry a $3 million insurance policy. If your Brooklyn venue needs a certificate of insurance naming them as additionally insured, reply to your booking confirmation with their contact email and we'll send it over.
